---
id: scouting
label: Scouting Mishaps
source: User-provided excerpt of the Scouting (Wits) skill from Forbidden Lands; table assumes spotting approaching threats and identifying distant sights, not searching for hidden things
dice: D66
version: 1
---

## Rows

| dice | result | effect | severity | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 11-13 | False Alarm | You mistake shadows, birds, or brush movement for a threat. The group loses time reacting to nothing. | Low |  |
| 14-16 | Distant Blur | You spot something far away but cannot tell what it is. You gain only confusion, not clarity. | Low |  |
| 21-23 | Eyestrain | You stare too long into glare, fog, or dimness. Suffer 1 point of damage to Wits from strain and frustration. | Moderate |  |
| 24-26 | Missed Approach | You are watching the wrong direction. An enemy or beast closes distance before the group is warned. | High |  |
| 31-33 | Bad Signal | You warn your allies too late or too unclearly. They are disorganized when danger arrives. | Moderate |  |
| 34-36 | Silhouette Error | You mistake a harmless traveler, patrol, or animal for a deadly threat. A tense encounter begins on the wrong footing. | Moderate |  |
| 41-43 | Exposed Position | While trying for a better look, you reveal yourself on a ridge, roof, or treeline. Anyone out there can now spot you as well. | High |  |
| 44-46 | Chasing Movement | You fixate on one suspicious sight and miss the real danger elsewhere. The GM introduces a second threat at close range. | High |  |
| 51-53 | Ambush Walk-In | You fail to recognize the signs of an ambush until it is sprung. Opponents gain the initiative. | Severe |  |
| 54-56 | Friendly Misfire | Your report identifies the wrong target or threat. Allies act on faulty information and create immediate complications. | High |  |
| 61-63 | Panic Warning | You announce danger with such certainty that the group bolts, scatters, or gives away its location. Everyone loses position. | Severe |  |
| 64-66 | Blind to the Kill | You fail at the one warning that mattered. A hidden or distant threat strikes decisively before anyone can prepare. | Catastrophic |  |
